1	# Reconstructed proof chain
     2	
     3	The following blocks formalize the supplied continuous proof. All estimates are asserted with their quantifiers and their proof blocks record the exact interfaces used by the argument.
     4	
     5	::: {#def-admissible-polygon .definition name="Admissible simple polygon" date="2026-10-31" status="verified"}
     6	An admissible polygon is a bounded simple planar polygonal domain whose boundary is a simple cyclic union of finitely many nonzero straight segments, with no self-contact. A genuine corner is a boundary vertex at which the two incident directed segments are not collinear; its interior angle is required to lie strictly between $0$ and $2\pi$. Starting from any polygonal presentation, delete adjacent collinear redundant vertices cyclically until no such vertex remains; the resulting effective-edge count is the invariant number $N$, and $A(P)$ is the Euclidean area.
     7	:::
     8	
     9	::: {#def-j-functional .definition name="Area-eigenvalue functional" date="2026-10-31" status="verified"}
    10	For an admissible polygon $P$ in @def-admissible-polygon, let $\lambda_1(P)$ be the first Dirichlet eigenvalue of $-\Delta$ on the bounded nondegenerate polygonal domain $P$ and define
    11	$$
    12	J(P)=A(P)\lambda_1(P),\qquad
    13	m_k=\inf\{J(Q):Q\text{ is admissible and has at most }k\text{ effective edges}\}.
    14	$$
    15	Here $k\ge3$ is an integer, and $R_k$ denotes the unit-area regular $k$-gon (its position is irrelevant because $J$ is similarity invariant). The first eigenvalue is defined by the Dirichlet Rayleigh quotient on $H_0^1(P)$.
    16	:::
    17	
    18	::: {#def-stationary-polygon .definition name="Vertex stationary polygon" date="2026-10-31"}
    19	An admissible polygon in @def-admissible-polygon is stationary when, in a differentiable local chart of its effective vertex coordinates, $DJ(P)[V]=0$ for every vertex variation $V$. On the same chart this is equivalent to $D\lambda_1(P)[V]=0$ for every variation with $DA(P)[V]=0$: the forward implication follows from $DJ=A\,D\lambda_1+\lambda_1,DA$, and the converse follows by applying the scaling identities $D\lambda_1[X]=-2\lambda_1$ and $DA[X]=2A$ to the radial variation and then using the Lagrange-multiplier decomposition.
    20	:::
    21	
    22	::: {#def-conformal-data .definition name="Normalized conformal data" date="2026-10-31"}
    23	For a polygon $P$ in @def-admissible-polygon, let $r_P$ be its maximal conformal radius and choose a Riemann map $F:\mathbb D\to P$ centered at a maximizing point, with $F'(0)=r_P>0$ and $F''(0)=0$. The equality $F''(0)=0$ is the first-order condition for the maximum of $(1-|a|^2)|F'(a)|$. Replace $P$ by the similarity-normalized polygon $\widetilde P=r_P^{-1}(P-F(0))$ and write $\widetilde F=r_P^{-1}(F-F(0))$; this leaves $J$ and the effective-edge count unchanged and gives $\widetilde F'(0)=1$. In the normalized notation,
    24	$$
    25	\widetilde F'(z)=1+g(z),\qquad g(z)=\sum_{n\ge2}g_nz^n.
    26	$$
    27	Set
    28	$$
    29	S=\|g\|_{A^2}^2=\sum_{n\ge2}\frac{|g_n|^2}{n+1},\qquad
    30	T=\|(\widetilde F')^{-1}-1\|_{A^2}^2,\qquad \|h\|_{A^2}^2=\pi^{-1}\int_{\mathbb D}|h|^2dA.
    31	$$
    32	The area identity is $A(\widetilde P)=\pi(1+S)$; all later uses of $P,F,A,\lambda_1$ are understood in this similarity-normalized representative.
    33	:::
    34	
    35	::: {#def-turn-measure .definition name="Signed Schwarz-Christoffel turn measure" date="2026-10-31"}
    36	At the prevertices $e^{i\theta_i}$ of an admissible polygon in @def-admissible-polygon, with normalized conformal map from @def-conformal-data, put
    37	$$
    38	w_i=\frac{\pi-\omega_i}{2\pi},\qquad
    39	\mu=\sum_iw_i\delta_{\theta_i},\qquad \widehat\mu(n)=\int e^{-in\theta}d\mu(\theta).
    40	$$
    41	Then $\sum_iw_i=1$ and $\widehat\mu(1)=0$ in the chosen $F''(0)=0$ normalization. The Schwarz--Christoffel derivative has logarithm
    42	$$
    43	L(z)=\log F'(z)=2\sum_{n\ge1}\frac{\widehat\mu(n)}n z^n,
    44	$$
    45	so $L_n=2\widehat\mu(n)/n$. This definition applies to finite real atomic measures induced by such polygons; all Fourier series below are interpreted in that class.
    46	:::
    47	
    48	::: {#def-positive-kernel .definition name="Positive comparison kernel" date="2026-10-31"}
    49	Let $j=j_{0,1}$ be the first positive zero of the Bessel function $J_0$, let $\kappa=j^2/2-1>0$, and define for $n\ge1$
    50	$$
    51	b_n=\frac1{n(n^2+\kappa)},\qquad
    52	E_b(\mu)=\sum_{n\ge1}b_n|\widehat\mu(n)|^2,
    53	$$
    54	for a finite real atomic measure $\mu$ of total mass $1$ as in @def-turn-measure. For every positive integer $p$, set
    55	$$
    56	B_p=\sum_{\ell\ge1}\frac1{\ell p((\ell p)^2+\kappa)}.
    57	$$
    58	The series defining $E_b$ and $B_p$ converge absolutely because $b_n=O(n^{-3})$ and finite atomic measures have bounded Fourier coefficients.
    59	:::
    60	
    61	::: {#lem-edge-moments .lemma name="Stationary edge moments" date="2026-10-31"}
    62	Let $P$ be admissible and stationary in the sense of @def-stationary-polygon. If $u>0$ is the $L^2$-normalized first eigenfunction, $\lambda=\lambda_1(P)$, $c=\lambda/A(P)$, and $q=|\partial_\nu u|^2$, then every effective edge $E$, parametrized by physical arclength $s\in[0,\ell_E]$, satisfies
    63	$$
    64	\int_E(q-c)\,ds=0,\qquad \int_Es(q-c)\,ds=0.
    65	$$
    66	:::
    67	
    68	::: {.proof of="lem-edge-moments"}
    69	By @def-stationary-polygon, the derivative of $J=A\lambda$ vanishes for every vertex displacement. Hadamard's formula is
    70	$$
    71	DJ[V]=A\int_{\partial P}(c-q)V\cdot\nu\,ds.
    72	$$
    73	Moving one endpoint of an effective edge while keeping the other fixed produces an affine normal velocity on that edge, and the two endpoint velocities give the independent functions $1$ and $s/\ell_E$. Since adjacent effective edge normals are linearly independent at a genuine corner, stationarity forces both coefficients of these two affine test functions to vanish. Rescaling $s/\ell_E$ gives the displayed moments.
    74	:::
    75	
    76	::: {#lem-airy-identity .lemma name="Airy fourth-power identity" date="2026-10-31"}
    77	Under the hypotheses of @lem-edge-moments, the first eigenfunction satisfies
    78	$$
    79	\int_P|\nabla u|^4=\lambda^2\left(\int_Pu^4-A(P)^{-1}\right).
    80	$$
    81	:::
    82	
    83	::: {.proof of="lem-airy-identity"}
    84	Define the divergence-free stress tensor
    85	$$
    86	T=\nabla u\otimes\nabla u-\tfrac12(|\nabla u|^2-\lambda u^2)I.
    87	$$
    88	An Airy potential $\psi$ with $D^2\psi=R^TTR$ exists locally and, after setting $\Phi=\psi-c|x|^2/4$, satisfies
    89	$$
    90	D^2\Phi=\tfrac12(|\nabla u|^2+\lambda u^2-c)I-\nabla u\otimes\nabla u.
    91	$$
    92	On each open edge, the two identities in @lem-edge-moments imply $\nabla\Phi$ has the same endpoint values. Propagating around the boundary and subtracting an affine function makes $\Phi=0$ at every vertex and $\partial_\nu\Phi=0$ on every open edge; the mixed Hessian term vanishes there as well. At a corner of angle $\omega<2\pi$, the leading Dirichlet mode is $r^\alpha\sin(\alpha\theta)$ with $\alpha=\pi/\omega>1/2$. Thus $|\nabla u|^4$ is locally integrable and the boundary terms on circles of radius $\varepsilon$ tend to zero.
    93	
    94	Apply the divergence identity
    95	$$
    96	\operatorname{div}\{\Delta\Phi\nabla\Phi-D^2\Phi\nabla\Phi\}=(\Delta\Phi)^2-|D^2\Phi|^2
    97	$$
    98	to $P$ with corner disks removed and let $\varepsilon\downarrow0$. The edge terms vanish by the preceding boundary conditions, hence $\int_P\det D^2\Phi=0$. The eigenvalues of $D^2\Phi$ are $(\lambda u^2-c\pm|\nabla u|^2)/2$, so expanding their product and using $\int_Pu^2=1$ gives the stated identity.
    99	:::
   100	
   101	::: {#lem-uniform-w14 .lemma name="Uniform W1,4 bound" date="2026-10-31"}
   102	There is a universal constant such that every admissible stationary polygon with fixed area and bounded first eigenvalue has its zero extension of the normalized first eigenfunction uniformly bounded in $W^{1,4}(\mathbb R^2)$ and in $C^{0,1/2}(\mathbb R^2)$.
   103	:::
   104	
   105	::: {.proof of="lem-uniform-w14"}
   106	The heat-kernel estimate gives $\|u\|_\infty^2\le e^2\lambda/(8\pi)$. Combining this with @lem-airy-identity yields
   107	$$
   108	\int_P|\nabla u|^4\le \frac{e^2\lambda^3}{8\pi}.
   109	$$
   110	The $L^2$ normalization supplies the remaining $W^{1,4}$ terms. In the plane, the zero extension of an $H^1_0$ function with a uniform $W^{1,4}$ bound has a uniform $C^{0,1/2}$ representative by Morrey's inequality. The constants depend only on the area normalization and the upper bound for $\lambda$, not on corner angles or edge lengths.
   111	:::
   112	
   113	::: {#lem-near-circle-conformal .lemma name="Near-circle conformal deficit" date="2026-10-31"}
   114	For a sequence of admissible stationary $N$-gons satisfying
   115	$$
   116	J(P)\le J(R_{N-1}),
   117	$$
   118	with $N\to\infty$, the conformal data of @def-conformal-data satisfy $S\to0$ and, in fact, $S\le C N^{-3}$ with a universal $C$.
   119	:::
   120	
   121	::: {.proof of="lem-near-circle-conformal"}
   122	The regular-polygon asymptotic is
   123	$$
   124	\frac{J(R_M)}{\pi j^2}=1+\frac{4\zeta(3)}{M^3}+O(M^{-5}).
   125	$$
   126	After area normalization, the quantitative Faber--Krahn inequality and the assumed upper bound imply convergence in measure to the unit disk. By @lem-uniform-w14, normalized eigenfunctions converge uniformly on compact subsets; positivity of the disk eigenfunction then gives $B_{1-\eta}\subset P$ for every fixed $\eta>0$ and all sufficiently large $N$. The maximum conformal radius is therefore at least $1-\eta$ and at most $1$. In the normalization $F'(0)=1$, this yields $1+S=r_P^{-2}\to1$.
   127	
   128	For the quantitative rate, write the pulled-back eigenproblem as
   129	$$
   130	-\Delta v=\lambda|1+g|^2v,\qquad v|_{\partial\mathbb D}=0,
   131	$$
   132	with the weighted $L^2$ normalization. The disk Green operator on the zero-trace $C^1$ space satisfies
   133	$$
   134	\|\mathcal G(gh)\|_{C^1}\le C\|g\|_{A^2}\|h\|_{C^1},\qquad
   135	\|\mathcal G(g_1\overline{g_2}h)\|_{C^1}\le C\|g_1\|_{A^2}\|g_2\|_{A^2}\|h\|_{C^1}.
   136	$$
   137	Bergman pointwise bounds near the boundary and the Green kernel estimates prove these inequalities. Analytic perturbation around the simple disk ground state gives $v=v_0+v_1+v_2+O_X(S^{3/2})$ and
   138	$$
   139	\frac{J(P)}{\pi j^2}=1+S-\sum_{n\ge2}\frac{\rho_n}{(n+1)^2}|g_n|^2+O(S^{3/2}),
   140	\qquad \rho_n=j\frac{J_{n+1}(j)}{J_n(j)},\quad0<\rho_n<2.
   141	$$
   142	Thus the quadratic term is at least $S/3$ and, after shrinking the universal small neighborhood, $J(P)/(\pi j^2)-1\ge S/6$. The upper bound is $O(N^{-3})$, hence $S\le CN^{-3}$.
   143	:::
   144	
   145	::: {#lem-inverse-energy .lemma name="Inverse derivative energy" date="2026-10-31"}
   146	For the conformal data in @def-conformal-data of a stationary polygon in the regime of @lem-near-circle-conformal, one has
   147	$$
   148	T\le CS.
   149	$$
   150	The constant is independent of the number and separation of the vertices and of the angle sizes.
   151	:::
   152	
   153	::: {.proof of="lem-inverse-energy"}
   154	Pull @lem-airy-identity back by $F$ and use $F'^{-1}=1+k$ to obtain
   155	$$
   156	\int_{\mathbb D}|\nabla v|^4|1+k|^2
   157	=\lambda^2\int_{\mathbb D}v^4|1+g|^2-\frac{\lambda^2}{\pi(1+S)}.
   158	$$
   159	The perturbation expansion in @lem-near-circle-conformal gives $|\nabla v|^4=a+b_1+O(S)$, where $a=|\nabla v_0|^4$ is radial and $b_1$ has zero circular mean. Since the constant Fourier mode of $k$ is zero, orthogonality leaves a term $\int a|k|^2$ on the left. On a fixed outer annulus $a$ is bounded below, while $k=-g/(1+g)=O(\sqrt S)$ on the inner disk. Cauchy--Schwarz and the perturbation bounds therefore give
   160	$$
   161	T\le C\{S+\sqrt S\sqrt T+\sqrt S\,T+ST\}.
   162	$$
   163	Young's inequality absorbs the mixed term and, for sufficiently small $S$, the last two terms, proving $T\le CS$.
   164	:::
   165	
   166	::: {#lem-spectral-core .lemma name="Uniform nonlinear spectral lower bound" date="2026-10-31"}
   167	There are universal constants $C$ and $S_0>0$ such that every stationary polygon in the regime of @lem-near-circle-conformal with $S\le S_0$ satisfies
   168	$$
   169	\frac{J(P)}{\pi j^2}\ge 1+4\sum_{n\ge2}a_n|\widehat\mu(n)|^2-C S^{3/2}\sqrt{\log(e/S)},
   170	$$
   171	where @def-turn-measure defines $\mu$ and
   172	$$
   173	a_n=\frac{\beta_n}{n^2(n+1)^2}\left(1+\frac{\beta_n}{n^2-1}\right),
   174	\qquad \beta_n=n+1-j\frac{J_{n+1}(j)}{J_n(j)}.
   175	$$
   176	:::
   177	
   178	::: {.proof of="lem-spectral-core"}
   179	The first-order perturbation and the second-order disk calculation from @lem-near-circle-conformal give
   180	$$
   181	\frac{J(P)}{\pi j^2}=1+S-\sum_{n\ge2}\frac{\rho_n}{(n+1)^2}|g_n|^2+O(S^{3/2}),
   182	$$
   183	with $\beta_n=n+1-\rho_n$. By @lem-inverse-energy, $T\le CS$. The identity $g+k=-gk$ gives weighted coefficient bounds; splitting at $K=S^{-1/2}$ yields, for every multiplier $O((n+1)^{-2})$,
   184	$$
   185	\left|\sum b_n(|k_n|^2-|g_n|^2)\right|\le CS^{3/2}\sqrt{\log(e/S)}.
   186	$$
   187	The same bound replaces $g$ by $L=\log F'$ in all such quadratic forms, while the leading $T-S$ term is retained.
   188	
   189	To compute that leading term, introduce the Airy potential from @lem-airy-identity and the two-variable analytic functional obtained by treating $g$ and $k$ independently. Its quadratic part is computed on a polynomial direction $F'(z)=1+ta z^n$. The first-order boundary flux is
   190	$$
   191	\delta(q-c)=-\frac{2p_D^2\beta_n}{n+1}\operatorname{Re}(ae^{in\theta}),
   192	\qquad p_D=j/\sqrt\pi.
   193	$$
   194	The induced first-order Airy gradient has frequencies $n+1$ and $1-n$; its signed area is $-\pi d_n^2/[8(n^2-1)]$. Since the Airy identity equals minus four times this area, the quadratic contribution is
   195	$$
   196	2\pi p_D^4\frac{\beta_n^2}{(n+1)^2(n^2-1)}|a|^2.
   197	$$
   198	Rotational orthogonality removes cross terms, and density of analytic polynomials extends the calculation to $A^2$. The actual relation $g+k=-gk$ then gives
   199	$$
   200	S-T=2\sum_{n\ge2}\frac{\beta_n^2}{(n+1)^2(n^2-1)}|g_n|^2+O(S^{3/2}\sqrt{\log(e/S)}).
   201	$$
   202	The logarithmic inequality
   203	$$
   204	\|L\|_{A^2}^2\le (S+T)/2
   205	$$
   206	comes from $|f|^2+|f|^{-2}-2\ge4(\operatorname{Re}L)^2$ and equality of real and imaginary Bergman energies. Combining these formulas gives
   207	$$
   208	\frac{J(P)}{\pi j^2}\ge1+\sum_{n\ge2}\frac{\beta_n}{(n+1)^2}\left(1+\frac{\beta_n}{n^2-1}\right)|L_n|^2-C S^{3/2}\sqrt{\log(e/S)}.
   209	$$
   210	Finally @def-turn-measure gives $L_n=2\widehat\mu(n)/n$, which is the claimed inequality.
   211	:::
   212	
   213	::: {#lem-toeplitz-positive-atoms .lemma name="Positive-atom Toeplitz bound" date="2026-10-31"}
   214	Let $\mu$ be a finite real atomic measure of total mass $1$ with exactly $p$ positive atoms, allowing arbitrary negative atoms. For $0<\tau<1$,
   215	$$
   216	\sum_{n\ge1}\tau^n|\widehat\mu(n)|^2\ge\frac{\tau^p}{1-\tau^p}.
   217	$$
   218	:::
   219	
   220	::: {.proof of="lem-toeplitz-positive-atoms"}
   221	Define on $\ell^2(\mathbb N_0)$ the self-adjoint matrix
   222	$$
   223	A_{rs}=\tau^{(r+s)/2}\widehat\mu(r-s)=\sum_iw_i(v_i)_r\overline{(v_i)_s},
   224	\qquad (v_i)_r=\tau^{r/2}e^{-ir\theta_i}.
   225	$$
   226	The Vandermonde vectors at distinct nodes are linearly independent, so $A$ has exactly $p$ positive eigenvalues $\alpha_1\ge\cdots\ge\alpha_p>0$. The trace is $(1-\tau)^{-1}$, while the shift compression gives $\alpha_{i+1}\le\tau\alpha_i$. Comparing the positive spectrum with the length-$p$ geometric sequence having the same sum and applying summation by parts gives
   227	$$
   228	\sum_i\alpha_i^2\ge \frac{1+\tau}{1-\tau}\frac{\tau^p}{1-\tau^p}\quad\text{after the trace lower bound is inserted}.
   229	$$
   230	On the other hand,
   231	$$
   232	\|A\|_{HS}^2=\frac{1+2\sum_{n\ge1}\tau^n|\widehat\mu(n)|^2}{1-\tau^2}
   233	$$
   234	and the Hilbert--Schmidt norm dominates the squared positive eigenvalues. Rearranging yields the claimed bound.
   235	:::
   236	
   237	::: {#lem-kernel-comparison .lemma name="Positive kernel comparison" date="2026-10-31"}
   238	For every $n\ge2$, the coefficients in @lem-spectral-core satisfy
   239	$$
   240	0<b_n\le a_n.
   241	$$
   242	Moreover,
   243	$$
   244	b_n=\int_0^\infty e^{-nt}\frac{1-\cos(\sqrt\kappa t)}\kappa\,dt,
   245	$$
   246	so for any signed atomic measure of total mass $1$ with $p$ positive atoms,
   247	$$
   248	E_b(\mu)\ge B_p.
   249	$$
   250	:::
   251	
   252	::: {.proof of="lem-kernel-comparison"}
   253	The Bessel bounds $5.78<j^2<5.8$ give $1.89<\kappa<1.9$. The recurrence for $J_n$ implies $0<\rho_n<2$ and, for $n\ge3$, $\rho_n<n\alpha/(n^2+\kappa)$ with $\alpha=\kappa+1$. Substitution into
   254	$$
   255	a_n=\frac{n-\rho_n+\rho_n^2/(n+1)^2}{n^2(n^2-1)}
   256	$$
   257	proves $a_n\ge b_n$; for $n=2$, the identity $J_0(j)=0$ reduces the inequality to $\kappa^3+7\kappa^2+12\kappa-54\ge0$, which holds for $\kappa\ge1.89$.
   258	
   259	The Laplace representation follows from
   260	$$
   261	\int_0^\infty e^{-nt}(1-\cos(\sqrt\kappa t))\,dt=\frac{\kappa}{n(n^2+\kappa)}.
   262	$$
   263	Apply @lem-toeplitz-positive-atoms with $\tau=e^{-t}$ and integrate against the nonnegative weight $(1-\cos(\sqrt\kappa t))/\kappa$. Tonelli's theorem gives $E_b(\mu)\ge B_p$.
   264	:::
   265	
   266	::: {#lem-signed-turn-lower-bound .lemma name="Signed-turn spectral lower bound" date="2026-10-31"}
   267	For a stationary polygon in the regime of @lem-spectral-core, if $p$ is its number of convex corners, then
   268	$$
   269	\frac{J(P)}{\pi j^2}\ge1+4B_p-C S^{3/2}\sqrt{\log(e/S)}.
   270	$$
   271	:::
   272	
   273	::: {.proof of="lem-signed-turn-lower-bound"}
   274	By @lem-spectral-core and @lem-kernel-comparison, $a_n\ge b_n$ for $n\ge2$. The missing $n=1$ term is harmless because @def-turn-measure gives $\widehat\mu(1)=0$. Hence
   275	$$
   276	\frac{J(P)}{\pi j^2}ge1+4E_b(\mu)-C S^{3/2}\sqrt{\log(e/S)}.
   277	$$
   278	The lower bound $E_b(\mu)\ge B_p$ is exactly @lem-kernel-comparison.
   279	:::
   280	
   281	::: {#lem-two-reflex-exclusion .lemma name="At least two reflex corners are excluded" date="2026-10-31"}
   282	There is $N_1$ such that no stationary admissible $N$-gon with at least two reflex corners satisfies
   283	$$
   284	J(P)\le J(R_{N-1})
   285	$$
   286	for $N\ge N_1$.
   287	:::
   288	
   289	::: {.proof of="lem-two-reflex-exclusion"}

::: {#lem-near-circle-conformal .lemma name="Near-circle conformal deficit" date="2026-10-31"}
For a sequence of admissible stationary $N$-gons satisfying @lem-edge-moments and
$$
J(P)\le J(R_{N-1}),
$$
with $N\to\infty$, the conformal data of @def-conformal-data satisfy $S\to0$ and, in fact, $S\le C N^{-3}$ with a universal $C$.
:::

::: {.proof of="lem-near-circle-conformal"}
The regular-polygon asymptotic is
$$
\frac{J(R_M)}{\pi j^2}=1+\frac{4\zeta(3)}{M^3}+O(M^{-5}).
$$
After area normalization, the quantitative Faber--Krahn inequality and the assumed upper bound imply convergence in measure to the unit disk. By @lem-uniform-w14, normalized eigenfunctions converge uniformly on compact subsets; positivity of the disk eigenfunction then gives $B_{1-\eta}\subset P$ for every fixed $\eta>0$ and all sufficiently large $N$. The maximum conformal radius is therefore at least $1-\eta$ and at most $1$. In the normalization $F'(0)=1$, this yields $1+S=r_P^{-2}\to1$.

For the quantitative rate, write the pulled-back eigenproblem as
$$
-\Delta v=\lambda|1+g|^2v,\qquad v|_{\partial\mathbb D}=0,
$$
with the weighted $L^2$ normalization. The disk Green operator on the zero-trace $C^1$ space satisfies
$$
\|\mathcal G(gh)\|_{C^1}\le C\|g\|_{A^2}\|h\|_{C^1},\qquad
\|\mathcal G(g_1\overline{g_2}h)\|_{C^1}\le C\|g_1\|_{A^2}\|g_2\|_{A^2}\|h\|_{C^1}.
$$
Bergman pointwise bounds near the boundary and the Green kernel estimates prove these inequalities. Analytic perturbation around the simple disk ground state gives $v=v_0+v_1+v_2+O_X(S^{3/2})$ and
$$
\frac{J(P)}{\pi j^2}=1+S-\sum_{n\ge2}\frac{\rho_n}{(n+1)^2}|g_n|^2+O(S^{3/2}),
\qquad \rho_n=j\frac{J_{n+1}(j)}{J_n(j)},\quad0<\rho_n<2.
$$
Thus the quadratic term is at least $S/3$ and, after shrinking the universal small neighborhood, $J(P)/(\pi j^2)-1\ge S/6$. The upper bound is $O(N^{-3})$, hence $S\le CN^{-3}$.
:::

::: {#lem-inverse-energy .lemma name="Inverse derivative energy" date="2026-10-31"}
For the conformal data in @def-conformal-data of a stationary polygon satisfying @lem-edge-moments and in the regime of @lem-near-circle-conformal, one has
$$
T\le CS.
$$
The constant is independent of the number and separation of the vertices and of the angle sizes.
:::

::: {.proof of="lem-inverse-energy"}
Under the edge-moment hypotheses @lem-edge-moments, pull @lem-airy-identity back by $F$ and use $F'^{-1}=1+k$ to obtain
$$
\int_{\mathbb D}|\nabla v|^4|1+k|^2
=\lambda^2\int_{\mathbb D}v^4|1+g|^2-\frac{\lambda^2}{\pi(1+S)}.
$$
The perturbation expansion in @lem-near-circle-conformal gives $|\nabla v|^4=a+b_1+O(S)$, where $a=|\nabla v_0|^4$ is radial and $b_1$ has zero circular mean. Since the constant Fourier mode of $k$ is zero, orthogonality leaves a term $\int a|k|^2$ on the left. On a fixed outer annulus $a$ is bounded below, while $k=-g/(1+g)=O(\sqrt S)$ on the inner disk. Cauchy--Schwarz and the perturbation bounds therefore give
$$
T\le C\{S+\sqrt S\sqrt T+\sqrt S\,T+ST\}.
$$
Young's inequality absorbs the mixed term and, for sufficiently small $S$, the last two terms, proving $T\le CS$.
:::

If there are at least two reflex corners, the number $p$ of convex corners is at most $N-2$. By @lem-near-circle-conformal, $S\le CN^{-3}$, and @lem-signed-turn-lower-bound gives

# Reconstructed proof chain

The following blocks formalize the supplied continuous proof. All estimates are asserted with their quantifiers and their proof blocks record the exact interfaces used by the argument.

::: {#def-admissible-polygon .definition name="Admissible simple polygon" date="2026-10-31"}
An admissible polygon is a bounded simple planar polygonal domain whose boundary is a simple cyclic union of finitely many nonzero straight segments, with no self-contact. A genuine corner is a boundary vertex at which the two incident directed segments are not collinear; its interior angle is required to lie strictly between $0$ and $2\pi$. Starting from any polygonal presentation, delete adjacent collinear redundant vertices cyclically until no such vertex remains; the resulting effective-edge count is the invariant number $N$, and $A(P)$ is the Euclidean area.
:::

::: {#def-j-functional .definition name="Area-eigenvalue functional" date="2026-10-31"}
For an admissible polygon $P$ in @def-admissible-polygon, let $\lambda_1(P)$ be the first Dirichlet eigenvalue of $-\Delta$ on the bounded nondegenerate polygonal domain $P$ and define
$$
J(P)=A(P)\lambda_1(P),\qquad
m_k=\inf\{J(Q):Q\text{ is admissible and has at most }k\text{ effective edges}\}.
$$
Here $k\ge3$ is an integer, and $R_k$ denotes the unit-area regular $k$-gon (its position is irrelevant because $J$ is similarity invariant). The first eigenvalue is defined by the Dirichlet Rayleigh quotient on $H_0^1(P)$.
:::

::: {#def-stationary-polygon .definition name="Vertex stationary polygon" date="2026-10-31"}
An admissible polygon in @def-admissible-polygon, with $J$ as defined in @def-j-functional, is stationary when, in a differentiable local chart of its effective vertex coordinates, $DJ(P)[V]=0$ for every vertex variation $V$. On the same chart this is equivalent to $D\lambda_1(P)[V]=0$ for every variation with $DA(P)[V]=0$: the forward implication follows from $DJ=A\,D\lambda_1+\lambda_1\,DA$, and the converse follows by applying the scaling identities $D\lambda_1[X]=-2\lambda_1$ and $DA[X]=2A$ to the radial variation and then using the Lagrange-multiplier decomposition.
:::

::: {#def-conformal-data .definition name="Normalized conformal data" date="2026-10-31"}
For a polygon $P$ in @def-admissible-polygon, let $r_P$ be its maximal conformal radius and choose a Riemann map $F:\mathbb D\to P$ centered at a maximizing point, with $F'(0)=r_P>0$ and $F''(0)=0$. The equality $F''(0)=0$ is the first-order condition for the maximum of $(1-|a|^2)|F'(a)|$. Replace $P$ by the similarity-normalized polygon $\widetilde P=r_P^{-1}(P-F(0))$ and write $\widetilde F=r_P^{-1}(F-F(0))$; this leaves $J$ and the effective-edge count unchanged and gives $\widetilde F'(0)=1$. In the normalized notation,
$$
\widetilde F'(z)=1+g(z),\qquad g(z)=\sum_{n\ge2}g_nz^n.
$$
Set
$$
S=\|g\|_{A^2}^2=\sum_{n\ge2}\frac{|g_n|^2}{n+1},\qquad
T=\|(\widetilde F')^{-1}-1\|_{A^2}^2,\qquad \|h\|_{A^2}^2=\pi^{-1}\int_{\mathbb D}|h|^2dA.
$$
The area identity is $A(\widetilde P)=\pi(1+S)$; all later uses of $P,F,A,\lambda_1$ are understood in this similarity-normalized representative.
:::

::: {#def-turn-measure .definition name="Signed Schwarz-Christoffel turn measure" date="2026-10-31"}
At the prevertices $e^{i\theta_i}$ of an admissible polygon in @def-admissible-polygon, with normalized conformal map from @def-conformal-data, put
$$
w_i=\frac{\pi-\omega_i}{2\pi},\qquad
\mu=\sum_iw_i\delta_{\theta_i},\qquad \widehat\mu(n)=\int e^{-in\theta}d\mu(\theta).
$$
Then $\sum_iw_i=1$ and $\widehat\mu(1)=0$ in the chosen $F''(0)=0$ normalization. The Schwarz--Christoffel derivative has logarithm
$$
L(z)=\log F'(z)=2\sum_{n\ge1}\frac{\widehat\mu(n)}n z^n,
$$
so $L_n=2\widehat\mu(n)/n$. This definition applies to finite real atomic measures induced by such polygons; all Fourier series below are interpreted in that class.
:::

::: {#def-positive-kernel .definition name="Positive comparison kernel" date="2026-10-31"}
Let $j=j_{0,1}$ be the first positive zero of the Bessel function $J_0$, let $\kappa=j^2/2-1>0$, and define for $n\ge1$
$$
b_n=\frac1{n(n^2+\kappa)},\qquad
E_b(\mu)=\sum_{n\ge1}b_n|\widehat\mu(n)|^2,
$$
for a finite real atomic measure $\mu$ of total mass $1$ as in @def-turn-measure. For every positive integer $p$, set
$$
B_p=\sum_{\ell\ge1}\frac1{\ell p((\ell p)^2+\kappa)}.
$$
The series defining $E_b$ and $B_p$ converge absolutely because $b_n=O(n^{-3})$ and finite atomic measures have bounded Fourier coefficients.

$$

::: {#def-stationary-polygon .definition name="Vertex stationary polygon" date="2026-10-31"}
An admissible polygon in @def-admissible-polygon, with $J$ as defined in @def-j-functional, is stationary when, in a differentiable local chart of its effective vertex coordinates, $DJ(P)[V]=0$ for every vertex variation $V$. On the same chart this is equivalent to $D\lambda_1(P)[V]=0$ for every variation with $DA(P)[V]=0$: the forward implication follows from $DJ=A\,D\lambda_1+\lambda_1\,DA$, and the converse follows by applying the scaling identities $D\lambda_1[X]=-2\lambda_1$ and $DA[X]=2A$ to the radial variation and then using the Lagrange-multiplier decomposition.
:::

::: {#def-conformal-data .definition name="Normalized conformal data" date="2026-10-31"}
For a polygon $P$ in @def-admissible-polygon, let $r_P$ be its maximal conformal radius and choose a Riemann map $F:\mathbb D\to P$ centered at a maximizing point, with $F'(0)=r_P>0$ and $F''(0)=0$. The equality $F''(0)=0$ is the first-order condition for the maximum of $(1-|a|^2)|F'(a)|$. Replace $P$ by the similarity-normalized polygon $\widetilde P=r_P^{-1}(P-F(0))$ and write $\widetilde F=r_P^{-1}(F-F(0))$; this leaves $J$ and the effective-edge count unchanged and gives $\widetilde F'(0)=1$. In the normalized notation,
$$
\widetilde F'(z)=1+g(z),\qquad g(z)=\sum_{n\ge2}g_nz^n.
$$
Set
$$
S=\|g\|_{A^2}^2=\sum_{n\ge2}\frac{|g_n|^2}{n+1},\qquad
T=\|(\widetilde F')^{-1}-1\|_{A^2}^2,\qquad \|h\|_{A^2}^2=\pi^{-1}\int_{\mathbb D}|h|^2dA.
$$
The area identity is $A(\widetilde P)=\pi(1+S)$; all later uses of $P,F,A,\lambda_1$ are understood in this similarity-normalized representative.

::: {#lem-near-circle-conformal .lemma name="Near-circle conformal deficit" date="2026-10-31"}
For a sequence of admissible stationary $N$-gons in the sense of @def-stationary-polygon whose canonical boundary presentations consist entirely of effective edges, satisfying the edge moments of @lem-edge-moments and with $J,R$ as in @def-j-functional,
$$
J(P)\le J(R_{N-1}),
$$
with $N\to\infty$, the conformal data of @def-conformal-data satisfy $S\to0$ and, in fact, $S\le C N^{-3}$ with a universal $C$.
:::

::: {.proof .draft of="lem-near-circle-conformal"}
The regular-polygon asymptotic is
$$
\frac{J(R_M)}{\pi j^2}=1+\frac{4\zeta(3)}{M^3}+O(M^{-5}).
$$
After area normalization, the quantitative Faber--Krahn inequality and the assumed upper bound imply convergence in measure to the unit disk. By @lem-uniform-w14, normalized eigenfunctions converge uniformly on compact subsets; positivity of the disk eigenfunction then gives $B_{1-\eta}\subset P$ for every fixed $\eta>0$ and all sufficiently large $N$. The maximum conformal radius is therefore at least $1-\eta$ and at most $1$. In the normalization $F'(0)=1$, this yields $1+S=r_P^{-2}\to1$.

For the quantitative rate, write the pulled-back eigenproblem as
$$
-\Delta v=\lambda|1+g|^2v,\qquad v|_{\partial\mathbb D}=0,
$$
with the weighted $L^2$ normalization. The disk Green operator on the zero-trace $C^1$ space satisfies
$$
\|\mathcal G(gh)\|_{C^1}\le C\|g\|_{A^2}\|h\|_{C^1},\qquad
\|\mathcal G(g_1\overline{g_2}h)\|_{C^1}\le C\|g_1\|_{A^2}\|g_2\|_{A^2}\|h\|_{C^1}.
$$
Bergman pointwise bounds near the boundary and the Green kernel estimates prove these inequalities. Analytic perturbation around the simple disk ground state gives $v=v_0+v_1+v_2+O_X(S^{3/2})$ and
$$
\frac{J(P)}{\pi j^2}=1+S-\sum_{n\ge2}\frac{\rho_n}{(n+1)^2}|g_n|^2+O(S^{3/2}),
\qquad \rho_n=j\frac{J_{n+1}(j)}{J_n(j)},\quad0<\rho_n<2.
$$
Thus the quadratic term is at least $S/3$ and, after shrinking the universal small neighborhood, $J(P)/(\pi j^2)-1\ge S/6$. The upper bound is $O(N^{-3})$, hence $S\le CN^{-3}$.
:::

Substitution of $w_n$ and one integration by parts reduce this to
$$

\qquad \rho_n=j\frac{J_{n+1}(j)}{J_n(j)},\qquad 0<\rho_n<2.

=\frac{J_{n+1}(j)}{2\sqrt\pi(n+1)},

$$
v=v_0+t v_1+t^2v_2+O_{H^1_0}(t^3),

Use the similarity invariance in @def-j-functional to normalize $A(P)=\pi$ and translate so that the Fraenkel-optimal comparison disk is $D=B_1(0)$. The regular-polygon asymptotic is
$$
\frac{J(R_M)}{\pi j^2}=1+\frac{4\zeta(3)}{M^3}+O(M^{-5}).
$$
The upper bound and the displayed asymptotic give $\lambda_1(P)\le j^2(1+CN^{-3})$, while Faber--Krahn gives $\lambda_1(P)\ge j^2$. Quantitative Faber--Krahn therefore gives $|P\triangle D|\to0$. Let $u_N$ be the normalized positive eigenfunction and extend it by zero. By @lem-uniform-w14, the extensions are uniformly bounded in $W^{1,4}(\mathbb R^2)$ and hence equicontinuous and uniformly bounded. Arzelà--Ascoli gives a locally uniform limit along a subsequence. On every compact set outside $\overline D$, the limit must vanish: otherwise the uniform Hölder bound would force a fixed positive amount of area in $P_N\setminus D$, contradicting $|P_N\triangle D|\to0$. The same argument gives zero trace on $\partial D$. Since $\|u_N\|_\infty$ is uniformly bounded, the mass outside $D$ tends to zero; hence the limit has $L^2(D)$ norm one. Weak lower semicontinuity gives $\int_D|\nabla u|^2\le\liminf\lambda_1(P_N)=j^2$, while the disk Rayleigh inequality gives the reverse inequality. Thus the limit is the normalized positive disk eigenfunction $u_0$. Uniqueness of the limit upgrades the whole sequence to local uniform convergence, and the boundary Hölder bound upgrades it to uniform convergence on $\overline D$. Since $u_0>0$ on $B_{1-\eta}$, eventually $u_N>0$ there; because the zero extension vanishes off $P_N$, $B_{1-\eta}\subset P_N$.

The maximal conformal radius is at least $1-\eta$ by monotonicity under inclusion and at most $1$ by the conformal area inequality $A(P)\ge\pi r_P^2$. In the normalization of @def-conformal-data, $1+S=r_P^{-2}\to1$.

$$
\frac{J(P)}{\pi j^2}-1\ge S/6.

There are universal constants $S_0,C>0$ such that, for normalized conformal data from @def-conformal-data with $S\le S_0$, if $v$ is the positive first solution of

then, with $J$ as in @def-j-functional,

\frac{J(P)}{\pi j^2}=1+S-\sum_{n\ge2}\frac{\rho_n}{(n+1)^2}|g_n|^2+R(g),qquad |R(g)|\le CS^{3/2},
$$

$$
\frac{J(P)}{\pi j^2}-1\ge S/6.
$$

::: {.proof of="lem-disk-perturbation" status="verified"}

=\frac{J_{n+1}(j)}{2\sqrt\pi(n+1)},

本目录把附件 `source-original.md` 重建为 `workspace/large-n-proof.qmd`，并用 qmd-prover 的独立 `codex` 检查器配置进行检查：`model: gpt-6.1-sol`、`effort: high`、`citations: standard`、`rigor: standard`。项目保留默认的 unrestricted 外部数学基准；所有非平凡外部结果都在证明文本中点名。

机械检查的最终结果是：21 个语义事实、0 个结构错误、0 个循环、0 个未解析引用；其中 7 个事实因 `.draft` 保持 `open`，其余 14 个尚待独立检查。渲染准备也成功生成了 `.qmd-prover/generated/proof-status.qmd` 和依赖图。

检查器曾对基础定义和 `@lem-edge-moments` 给出通过 verdict；这些记录在后续源文件/外部基准变更后由 qmd-prover 标记为 stale，不能当作当前最终版本的已验证状态。修复后的 `@lem-toeplitz-positive-atoms` 当前缓存检查仍为 `verified`。

Toeplitz 引理的原稿确有错误。原稿写的正谱平方和下界系数不成立；例如 $p=1,\tau=0.9$ 时右端超过实际平方和。已改为
$$
\sum_i\alpha_i^2\ge
\frac{1+\tau^p}{(1-\tau^2)(1-\tau^p)},
$$
并补上了压缩交错、正惯性和严格凸约束最小化的说明。该修复后的引理由 `gpt-6.1-sol/high` 独立检查通过。

原稿中以下接口仍不能诚实地标为已证，因此在 QMD 中保留 `.draft`，主定理也保持 `open`：

- Airy 四次恒等式的全局势函数拼接和角点通量极限；
- 由统一 $W^{1,4}$ 界推出圆盘内包含及统一 $S\le CN^{-3}$ 的近圆定量步骤；
- 加入了独立的 `@lem-disk-perturbation`，把近圆谱展开拆成单独引理，并将 Green 估计改为固定 $H^1_0$ 形式估计；检查器曾对该引理给出 verified，但后续为修复梯度接口而修改了源块，当前缓存需重新确认。

- 非线性谱下界；
- 单反角小正原子和删除步骤；
- 依赖上述接口的主命题。

其中检查器明确指出：仅有统一 $W^{1,4}$ 界不能直接推出特征函数一致收敛和圆盘内包含；现在已补上紧性、极限识别和内圆包含的定性步骤。谱展开已改用固定 $H^1_0$ 上的形式扰动框架；检查器认为该标量展开在上一版本中可接受，但指出统一余项、Bessel 比值和复模态延拓仍有形式化缺口。检查器还指出原 Airy 证明把“有效边”直接当成所有开边，并且只说局部 Airy 势，未给出全局势和角点边界通量估计。上述问题已在重建稿中补充为显式假设、外部基准或待完成的 draft 接口；没有把它们伪装成已验证结论。

$$
(-\Delta-j^2)r=f,\qquad r|_{\partial\mathbb D}=0,\qquad \int_{\mathbb D}rv_0=0
$$

::: {.proof of="lem-weighted-disk-resolvent"}
Define $\mathcal H$ as the completion of measurable $f$ under the norm
$$
\|f\|_{\mathcal H}=\sup\left\{\left|\int_{\mathbb D}f\phi\right|:\phi\in H^1_0(\mathbb D),\ \|\nabla\phi\|_{L^{4/3}}\le1\right\}.
$$
The disk Green kernel satisfies the boundary-adapted estimate
$$
|\nabla_xG(x,y)|\le C\left(|x-y|^{-1}+\frac{d(y)}{|x-y|^2}\right).

$$
\|\nabla G[(h+\bar h)v_0]\|_{L^4}+\|G[(h+\bar h)v_0]\|_{L^4}\le C,
$$
while the same calculation with a factor $u$ or with $|h|^2v_0$ gives
$$
\|G[f]\|_{W^{1,4}}\le C\|f\|_{\mathcal H}.
$$

\[

=1+S-\sum_{n\ge2}\frac{\rho_n}{(n+1)^2}|g_n|^2

\tag{3.9}

Bessel 递推给 0<ρ_n<2，故 β_n≥n−1，二次型至少为 S/3。缩小统一小 S 范围后，有 Jcal−1≥S/6。结合此前已证明 S→0 及低谱上界，得到

\[
\boxed{S\le CN^{-3}.}
\tag{3.10}

\[

\tag{3.A2}

\[
\int_{|x-z|<\delta/2}|\nabla_xG_D|\,|g_1g_2h|dA
\le C\frac{\|g_1\|\|g_2\|\|h\|_X}{\delta}

\tag{3.A3}

\[

\tag{3.A4}
\]

\[

\le S\int_D|\nabla h|^2dA,
\qquad h\in H_0^1(D).
\tag{3.A6}

## Project setup

The user normally adds the `qmd-prover` skill and asks the agent in natural language to initialize the current project. The engine is the `qmd-prover` command, installed once on the host's `PATH`; the skill supplies these instructions. Run it from the project root:

```bash
qmd-prover init
```

If the command is not found, the tool is not installed — install it as described in the skill's `SKILL.md` before continuing.

The command reports any existing `AGENTS.md`, QMD sources, Quarto configuration, `.qmd-prover` state, and external-basis mode. If it returns `intent-required`, summarize what exists and ask whether the user wants to adopt those files in place, inspect them first, or leave them unchanged. Run `--adopt-existing` only after the user chooses adoption.

With no existing project content, the command creates a root `AGENTS.md` with the canonical managed block. It is idempotent when the current block is already present. If `AGENTS.md` exists without the block, preserve it and ask before rerunning with `--append-contract`. If it contains an older or different managed block, ask before using `--sync-contract`; synchronization replaces only that block. Put local project rules outside the managed block.

Whenever it writes, the command also scaffolds `.qmd-prover/` and, if the project has no Quarto configuration at all, a `_quarto.yml` that renders the project as a book. An existing Quarto configuration is preserved untouched; the result reports which happened.

Setup requires no QMD scaffold or initial theorem, and proving a goal requires no per-goal setup either: a protected goal with no proof yet is simply open.

## External mathematical basis

Before writing or checking mathematics, read `.qmd-prover/.external.qmd` if it exists. It is project-owned ordinary QMD controlling which results may be taken from outside the project:

| State | Meaning |
|---|---|
| file absent | External results are unrestricted. Identify them precisely and check every hypothesis. |
| file present but whitespace-only | Use no external mathematical results; develop every needed result in the project. |
| file has content | Use only the external results or classes of results allowed by that content. |

Equivalently: An absent file permits external mathematics subject to precise hypothesis checks; a whitespace-only file permits none; a nonempty file permits only its stated basis.

The agent may revise this file when the user's request or the developing proof context requires a different external basis, but it must make that change explicit. The exact content is verifier context. Any change invalidates affected verification cache keys and requires the relevant facts to be checked again.

The external basis is the only channel for outside mathematical premises. It does not create semantic graph nodes; every in-project premise is instead an ordinary `@id` dependency subject to import scope.

## Verification settings

Who checks the mathematics, and how strictly, is set in `.qmd-prover/config.yml` under `verification`; the skill's configuration reference defines every key, its accepted values, and its cost. Read the current file before proof work, choose these settings deliberately with the user rather than accepting whatever was scaffolded, and say which backend and which strictness levels were in force whenever you report a result.

Choose the backend from what the host actually has: `qmd-prover doctor` reports which CLI resolves and whether it is available. When both bundled adapters are usable, prefer the one that is *not* the agent developing the proofs, so the referee is a different system from the author.

Then raise strictness in stages as confidence grows, changing the settings only at a stage boundary:

1. **While the route is still being searched**, set `citations`, `rigor`, and `rigor-disprove` to `lenient` and keep `effort` default. A correct but informal argument is then accepted, so the verifier answers the question that matters at this stage — does this approach work at all — instead of returning long formality reports on steps that may be discarded tomorrow.
2. **Once the route holds end to end** and each proof is believed sound, move all three to `standard` and repair what the stricter pass finds. Do this before treating any result as settled: a `lenient` pass is weak evidence of rigor, and it is the point of the exercise to find the formality failures while they are still cheap to fix.
3. **When preparing the development for publication or handover**, use `strict` with a high `effort`, and expect more rejections and more tokens per check.

Never quietly walk a level back down to make a rejection disappear. If a proof fails at `standard`, repair the proof; lowering strictness only hides the finding, and re-lowering re-verifies the whole project anyway. `rigor-disprove` matters only once the project actually argues that a statement is false.

## qmd-prover contract

Every QMD file in the project is semantic mathematics compiled into one dependency graph; `.qmd-prover/` holds only derived tool state. Protected goal IDs begin `thm-main-`; every registered goal has exactly the classes `.theorem .goal`, a nonempty human-readable `name`, an ISO `date`, and a nonempty statement. Preserve its ID, `name`, classes, hypotheses, quantifiers, and statement body exactly. Edit pre-existing user files cautiously and only as the developing mathematics requires; never reformat prose that carries no semantic block.

A semantic declaration is a fenced Div with one stable ID, exactly one kind class, a nonempty `name`, an ISO introduction `date`, and a nonempty body. Its ID prefix must match its kind:

| Block | ID | Discipline |
|---|---|---|
| `.definition` | `def-*` | Introduce a term, object, or notation. The body is its construction; `@id` citations there are construction dependencies. Put any existence, uniqueness, or well-definedness argument in a linked proof. |
| `.lemma` | `lem-*` | State an auxiliary result. A lemma has the same proof standard as every other result. |
| `.proposition` | `prp-*` | State a useful standalone result that is not presented as a principal theorem. The distinction is expository only. |
| `.theorem` | `thm-*` | State a principal result and justify it in a separate linked proof. |
| `.corollary` | `cor-*` | State a consequence, but cite the earlier result explicitly in its linked proof. The label creates no dependency. |
| `.proof` | none | Justify exactly one declaration. Give it no ID; set `of` to the declaration ID and cite every logical dependency with `@id` at its point of use. |

A definition may have a linked proof when its construction needs justification. Every non-definition candidate needs one nonempty linked proof. A declaration and its linked proof normally remain in the same QMD file. The exception is a protected main goal: its declaration stays in the user's note, while its linked proof may live in any project file, such as `workspace/main-proof.qmd`.

Cite the defining declaration of any specialized term at its first load-bearing use. When a definition body or a linked proof relies on a term, object, or notation that is not standard mathematical vocabulary, cite its `@def-id` — or the `@id` of whatever result fixes it — at that point, so the dependency is recorded and the verifier can resolve the term against the cited construction. Standard vocabulary needs no citation, and the verifier is the authority on what counts as standard: the `verification.citations` setting (`lenient`, `standard`, or `strict`) governs how aggressively it scrutinizes terms and reports an uncited non-standard term as a gap, while `verification.rigor` governs how completely each proof step must be spelled out and `verification.rigor-disprove` does the same for a proposed refutation.

An `@id` citation records a logical dependency but does not make a declaration from another file available. Same-file citations need no scope metadata. Every cross-file dependency requires both of these steps:

1. In the producer file, export the declaration under its exact semantic ID:

```markdown
::: {#lem-local-class-group-finite .lemma name="Local class group is finite" date="2026-07-12" export="lem-local-class-group-finite"}
The local class group is finite.
:::

::: {.proof of="lem-local-class-group-finite"}
Give the proof here.
:::
```

2. In the consumer file, import that exact ID in the front matter:

```yaml
---
qmd-prover:
  imports:
    - from: foundations/local-groups.qmd
      use:
        - lem-local-class-group-finite
---
```

`from` is relative to the importing QMD file. Each `use` entry is one semantic ID, the producer must set `export` to that same ID, and wildcard or implicit imports are forbidden. Importing grants scope but does not itself declare a logical dependency: cite the imported result at its point of use. Do not add a separate `Uses` list. References in surrounding prose are navigational, and bibliographic citations such as `[@rudin1976]` remain ordinary Quarto citations.

In schematic form, the producer uses `export="<same-ID>"`, and the consumer imports that exact ID; `from` is relative to the consumer file.

Every explicit semantic ID is globally unique across the project. A linked `.proof of="thm-main-ID"` is an overlay for the protected target and is not a second declaration; never redeclare that target. Any fact may cite any other project fact, including a protected main goal, subject to the import scope rules above; global composition keeps dependents blocked until every cited fact is itself globally verified.

Workflow state for a proof lives in attributes on its `.proof` div, never in body prose. There are no reserved body markers: `OPEN`, `REJECTED`, `DISPROVED`, `VERIFIED`, and `REVOKED` are ordinary words with no meaning anywhere in QMD source. A definition may not carry `.disproof`; challenge an existence, uniqueness, or well-definedness claim in the linked theorem-like result that states it.

| Attribute | Written by | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| _none_ | — | An ordinary candidate, checked by default. |
| `.disproof` | author | The proof is a proposed counterexample or refutation of the exact theorem-like statement, checked in refutation mode. Conditional evidence until locally checked and globally composed. |
| `.draft` | author | The proof is deliberately unfinished. It is never sent to the verifier and the fact stays `open`. Remove the mark when the proof is ready to be checked. |
| `.assumed` | author | The fact is taken as given: never sent to the verifier, composed as `verified`, and recorded in the assumption footprint of everything that rests on it. On a `.proof` div with content the argument is trusted while its citations stay obligations; on a result div with no proof block the statement itself is trusted and the fact depends on nothing. Use it only for a claim you are prepared to stand behind unchecked, never for one that is merely unfinished. |
| `.abandon` | author | The proof is detached from its result and kept only for memory: never linked, never a competing proof, never checked. On a result div instead, it retires the whole fact. |
| `status` | engine | Display-only projection of the fact's local verdict (`verified`, `disproved`, or `rejected`), written by inspection. Never hand-write it; the engine overwrites or clears it and never reads it back. |

When more than one applies, `.abandon` outranks `.draft`, which outranks `.assumed`, which outranks `.disproof`. A definition or an assumed statement carries its attributes on its own div, because it has no proof block. `.assumed` may not be combined with `.draft` (a fact is taken as given or is unfinished, not both) or with `.disproof`; either collision makes the fact `broken`.

A proof carrying `.disproof` must give the actual counterexample or refutation, check the hypotheses, and explain why the stated conclusion fails. The verifier checks it conditionally on the exact direct dependency statements. A locally accepted refutation is conditional evidence; it becomes globally disproved only when machine analysis also establishes that its complete dependency closure is globally verified. A failed refutation is locally rejected. The verifier may also discover and report a counterexample while checking an ordinary candidate, without changing its QMD source.

Verification state lives in the project's exact verification cache and published snapshot as separate mechanical, local conditional, and global fields. Inspection also projects each checked fact's local verdict into a display-only `status` attribute on its div, but that attribute is excluded from every content hash, the verifier packet, the cache key, and the snapshot identity, and is never read back — so writing it can never change what is checked. Read global state from inspection, never from the `status` attribute.

## Rendered document

Every QMD file has two readers: the compiler, which checks the mathematics, and Quarto, which renders the document a person reads. A file can satisfy the first and still render wrongly, so these rules are part of writing the source, not a later formatting pass.

Write inline mathematics as `$…$` and display mathematics as `$$…$$` with the delimiters on their own lines. Never write `\(…\)` or `\[…\]`: the compiler accepts those, so every check still passes, but Quarto does not read single-backslash delimiters and renders the formula as literal parentheses or brackets. Convert any file that still uses them when you next edit it — except a protected main statement, which is the user's text: report the delimiters and let the user decide, since rewriting them changes the statement and breaks its lock.

`init` writes a `_quarto.yml` that renders the project as a Quarto book into `.qmd-prover/site/book`. Keep that layout: a book is the only Quarto layout in which result numbering runs across the whole project and an `@id` reference resolves to a declaration in another file. Rendered as separate documents instead, each file numbers its results from 1 and every cross-file reference renders as a question mark.

That configuration belongs to the project and qmd-prover never rewrites it, so its chapter list is yours to maintain. Add every QMD file you create to `book.chapters` in reading order and remove the entry when you delete the file. The first chapter is the book landing page and must be `index.qmd`; create one when the project has none. A file missing from the list is still compiled, checked, and part of the dependency graph — it is simply absent from the rendered book, and every reference into it renders as a question mark.

## Proof development in the project

Any file in any folder of the project is part of the same unified mathematics; folders are organizational structure for humans and agents, never a semantic boundary. By convention, put new agent-created definitions, intermediate results, proof attempts, calculations, examples, counterexamples, and planning notes under a `workspace/` folder in the project root, and organize files inside it however best serves the argument — by theme, by goal, or flat. Local project policy may suggest folder principles; imports and citations work identically across any layout.

- Maintain a progress note with the active route, proved frontier, open dependencies, and abandoned approaches when the development is large enough to need one.
- Put semantic definitions and intermediate results with their linked proofs in coherent subject QMD files.
- Put only the linked proof of a protected main goal in its proof overlay file, such as `workspace/main-proof.qmd`; do not repeat or rewrite the theorem.
- Follow every unproved dependency until it has its own proof. A plan, example, computation, or prose sketch is not a completed proof.
- Keep a failed route when it is useful for future work, but add `.abandon` to its `.proof` div so it is detached from its result and cannot silently become an active premise.
- Mark a proof you are still writing with `.draft` so it is not sent to the verifier, and remove the mark when it is ready to be checked. Mark `.assumed` only a fact you are prepared to stand behind unchecked; expect it in the assumption footprint of every goal above it.
- When a precise counterexample or refutation shows that a theorem-like statement is false, keep the statement unchanged, add `.disproof` to its linked `.proof` div, and submit the refutation to inspection.

After each coherent batch of semantic-QMD changes, run the narrowest useful inspection:

```bash
qmd-prover inspect fact @ID
qmd-prover inspect path PATH
qmd-prover inspect project
```

Fact and path inspection select the facts needed for the requested global result: the selected facts and their transitive local dependency closure. Every selected fact receives an independent local check when its exact target, proof, and direct dependency statements can be materialized. Reverse dependencies and unrelated facts are not checked. A full project inspection checks every fact.

Local verifier decisions, globally composed results, and refutation evidence remain under `.qmd-prover/` as persistent project state for later inspection and future paper-building. Never copy a proof, refutation, or the engine-written `status` attribute into a protected statement.

## Verification discipline

Passing one layer does not imply passing another:

| Layer | Enforced by | Covers |
|---|---|---|
| Mechanical | Compiler, project index, and inspector | Main-goal shape and locks, declaration shape, dates, IDs, imports, references, proof association, global uniqueness, dependency cycles, and snapshot freshness. This layer never reads an AI verdict. |
| Local conditional | Independent external verifier | Assuming the exact direct dependency statements are true, whether the submitted proof establishes the exact target, or whether the submitted refutation defeats it. The verifier does not inspect dependency proofs or states. |
| Global composition | Inspector over the dependency graph | A result is globally verified only when its mechanical layer passes, its local proof is accepted, and every direct dependency is globally verified. Cycles and unresolved edges make a fact `broken`, which prevents global verification. |
| Agent conduct | This contract | Project ownership, protected goals, the `workspace/` layout convention, accurate reporting, and response to verification findings. |

Machine dependency analysis and local AI verification have separate state. Machine analysis always builds the available graph and reports existence, scope, import/export, cycle, and source diagnostics without consulting AI. Local verification assumes only the supplied direct dependency conclusions and checks the proof that is actually stored; an unverified, rejected, or `broken` upstream proof does not suppress this local check. Only the verifier produces `verified`, `disproved`, or `rejected`; the mechanical layer may withdraw a recorded verdict when its inputs change, but never grants one. A local proof is accepted only with `verdict: "correct"`, no critical errors, and no gaps that the configured `rigor` treats as blocking. A local refutation is accepted only with `verdict: "disproved"`, a nonempty independently checkable refutation, no critical errors, and no gaps that the configured `rigor-disprove` treats as blocking. For an admissible polygon $P$ in @def-admissible-polygon, let $\lambda_1(P)$ be the first Dirichlet eigenvalue of $-\Delta$ on the bounded nondegenerate polygonal domain $P$ and define
$$
J(P)=A(P)\lambda_1(P),\qquad
m_k=\inf\{J(Q):Q\text{ is admissible and has at most }k\text{ effective edges}\}.

Here $k\ge3$ is an integer, and $R_k$ denotes the unit-area regular $k$-gon (its position is irrelevant because $J$ is similarity invariant). The first eigenvalue is defined by the Dirichlet Rayleigh quotient on $H_0^1(P)$.

::: {#def-stationary-polygon .definition name="Vertex stationary polygon" date="2026-10-31" status="verified"}
An admissible polygon in @def-admissible-polygon, with $J$ as defined in @def-j-functional, is stationary when, in a differentiable local chart of its effective vertex coordinates, $DJ(P)[V]=0$ for every vertex variation $V$. On the same chart this is equivalent to $D\lambda_1(P)[V]=0$ for every variation with $DA(P)[V]=0$: the forward implication follows from $DJ=A\,D\lambda_1+\lambda_1\,DA$, and the converse follows by applying the scaling identities $D\lambda_1[X]=-2\lambda_1$ and $DA[X]=2A$ to the radial variation and then using the Lagrange-multiplier decomposition.

::: {#def-conformal-data .definition name="Normalized conformal data" date="2026-10-31" status="verified"}
For a polygon $P$ in @def-admissible-polygon, let $r_P$ be its maximal conformal radius and choose a Riemann map $F:\mathbb D\to P$ centered at a maximizing point, with $F'(0)=r_P>0$ and $F''(0)=0$. Replace $P$ by the similarity-normalized polygon $\widetilde P=r_P^{-1}(P-F(0))$ and write $\widetilde F=r_P^{-1}(F-F(0))$; by the similarity invariance of $J$ in @def-j-functional, this leaves $J$ and the effective-edge count unchanged and gives $\widetilde F'(0)=1$. In the normalized notation,
$$
\widetilde F'(z)=1+g(z),\qquad g(z)=\sum_{n\ge2}g_nz^n.
$$
Set
$$
S=\|g\|_{A^2}^2=\sum_{n\ge2}\frac{|g_n|^2}{n+1},\qquad
T=\|(\widetilde F')^{-1}-1\|_{A^2}^2,\qquad \|h\|_{A^2}^2=\pi^{-1}\int_{\mathbb D}|h|^2dA.

::: {#lem-edge-moments .lemma name="Stationary edge moments" date="2026-10-31"}
Let $P$ be admissible and stationary in the sense of @def-stationary-polygon. If $u>0$ is the $L^2$-normalized first eigenfunction, $\lambda=\lambda_1(P)$, $c=\lambda/A(P)$, and $q=|\partial_\nu u|^2$, then every effective edge $E$, parametrized by physical arclength $s\in[0,\ell_E]$, satisfies
$$
\int_E(q-c)\,ds=0,\qquad \int_Es(q-c)\,ds=0.
$$
:::

::: {.proof of="lem-edge-moments" status="verified"}
By @def-stationary-polygon, the derivative of $J=A\lambda$ vanishes for every vertex displacement. Hadamard's formula is
$$
DJ[V]=A\int_{\partial P}(c-q)V\cdot\nu\,ds.
$$
Moving one endpoint of an effective edge while keeping the other fixed produces an affine normal velocity on that edge, and the two endpoint velocities give the independent functions $1$ and $s/\ell_E$. Since adjacent effective edge normals are linearly independent at a genuine corner, stationarity forces both coefficients of these two affine test functions to vanish. Rescaling $s/\ell_E$ gives the displayed moments.
:::

\int_P|\nabla u|^4=\lambda^2\left(\int_Pu^4-A(P)^{-1}\right).

::: {.proof of="lem-uniform-w14"}
The domain-independent Dirichlet heat-kernel estimate gives $\|u\|_\infty^2\le e^2\lambda/(8\pi)$ for the normalized first eigenfunction. Under the edge-moment hypotheses, @lem-airy-identity applies, and $\int_Pu^4\le\|u\|_\infty^2\int_Pu^2=\|u\|_\infty^2$; combining these facts yields
$$
\int_P|\nabla u|^4\le \frac{e^2\lambda^3}{8\pi}.
$$
The same $L^\infty$ bound gives $\int_P|u|^4\le\|u\|_\infty^2$, so the $W^{1,4}(P)$ norm is bounded by a constant depending only on $A_0$ and $\Lambda$. Since $u\in H^1_0(P)$, its zero extension has no boundary distribution term in its weak gradient; the extension therefore lies in $W^{1,4}(\mathbb R^2)$ with the same gradient bound. Morrey's inequality in dimension two then gives a $C^{0,1/2}$ representative with the same parameter dependence.
:::

::: {#lem-c1-perturbation .lemma name="Uniform C1 conformal perturbation" date="2026-11-02"}
Let
$$
X=\{\phi\in C^1(\overline{\mathbb D};\mathbb R):\phi|_{\partial\mathbb D}=0\},
\qquad \|\phi\|_X=\|\nabla\phi\|_{L^\infty}.
$$
For normalized conformal data from @def-conformal-data with $S=\|g\|_{A^2}^2$ sufficiently small, writing $g=t h$ with $t=\sqrt S$ and $\|h\|_{A^2}=1$, the pulled-back first eigenfunction has a uniform real-analytic expansion
$$
v=v_0+t v_1+v^{(2)}+R,
\qquad \|v_1\|_X\le C,
\qquad \|v^{(2)}\|_X\le CS,
\qquad \|R\|_X\le CS^{3/2},
$$
where $v_0(r)=J_0(jr)/(\sqrt\pi J_1(j))$, $v_1$ has no radial Fourier mode, and the corresponding eigenvalue branch is the positive first branch.
:::

::: {.proof of="lem-c1-perturbation" status="verified"}
By @def-conformal-data, $g$ is analytic, has no constant or linear coefficient, and satisfies $S=\|g\|_{A^2}^2$; its normalized conformal pullback is the weighted disk problem used below. Put $d(z)=1-|z|$. The Green kernel of the disk satisfies
$$
|\nabla_xG_D(x,z)|\le C|x-z|^{-1},
\qquad
|\nabla_xG_D(x,z)|\le C\frac{d(z)}{|x-z|^2}.
$$
The Bergman pointwise estimate gives $|g(z)|\le C\|g\|_{A^2}/d(z)$ for $g\in A^2$ with vanishing constant coefficient. If $h\in X$, then $|h(z)|\le d(z)\|h\|_X$. Splitting the Green integral into $|x-z|<d(x)/2$, the annulus $d(x)/2\le|x-z|<2d(x)$, and dyadic outer annuli, the two kernel bounds give
$$
\|G_D(gh)\|_X\le C\|g\|_{A^2}\|h\|_X,
\qquad
\|G_D(g_1\overline{g_2}h)\|_X\le C\|g_1\|_{A^2}\|g_2\|_{A^2}\|h\|_X.
$$
For example, in the near region $d(z)\simeq d(x)$ and the pointwise bounds leave an integrable $|x-z|^{-1}$ kernel; in the outer annuli $d(z)\le d(x)+|x-z|$ cancels one power of the second Green bound, and Cauchy--Schwarz gives $\|g_1g_2\|_{L^1}\le C\|g_1\|_{A^2}\|g_2\|_{A^2}$. Polynomial approximation extends these estimates to all $A^2$ data, and the Green potential has a continuous boundary derivative.

Define the real quadratic compact-operator family
$$
K_g h=G_D[|1+g|^2h]=G_D[h+2\operatorname{Re}(g)h+|g|^2h]
$$
onlinearly in $g$. The estimates give $\|K_g-K_0\|_{B(X)}\le C(\sqrt S+S)$. The operator $K_0$ is compact on $X$ by disk Poisson regularity and the compact embedding $C^{2,\alpha}(\overline{\mathbb D})\Subset C^1(\overline{\mathbb D})$. Its nonzero eigenvalues are the reciprocals of the Dirichlet eigenvalues; $1/j^2$ is an isolated simple eigenvalue.

Choose a fixed small contour $\Gamma$ enclosing only $1/j^2$. For $S$ small, the Neumann series uniformly bounds $(zI-K_g)^{-1}$ on $\Gamma$ and defines the rank-one Riesz projection
$$
\Pi_g=\frac1{2\pi i}\int_\Gamma(zI-K_g)^{-1}\,dz.
$$
The normalized vector
$$
\widetilde v(g)=\Pi_gv_0,
\qquad
v(g)=\frac{\widetilde v(g)}{\left(\int_{\mathbb D}\widetilde v(g)^2|1+g|^2\right)^{1/2}}
$$
therefore depends real-analytically on $g$ in a fixed $A^2$ neighborhood; the denominator stays uniformly away from zero. Writing $g=t h$, define $v_1=Dv(0)[h]$; its forcing has no radial Fourier mode because $h$ has no constant coefficient. The remaining Taylor terms give $v^{(2)}+R$, and Cauchy estimates on this fixed neighborhood give the displayed bounds with constants independent of the direction of $g$.

The form identity
$$
\int_{\mathbb D}|g|^2|\phi|^2\,dA
\le C\|g\|_{A^2}^2\int_{\mathbb D}|\nabla\phi|^2\,dA,
\qquad \phi\in H^1_0(\mathbb D),
$$
which follows from Hardy's inequality, shows that the pulled-back eigenfunction belongs to the weighted Dirichlet space and that the branch is the first Dirichlet branch. Since $v_0\ge c,d$ and $\|v-v_0\|_X\le C\sqrt S$, the branch is strictly positive in $\mathbb D$. This proves the lemma.
:::

::: {#lem-disk-perturbation .lemma name="Uniform disk perturbation expansion" date="2026-11-01"}
There are universal constants $S_0,C>0$ such that, for normalized conformal data from @def-conformal-data with $S\le S_0$, if $v$ is the positive first solution of
$$
-\Delta v=\lambda|1+g|^2v\quad\text{in }\mathbb D,qquad v|_{\partial\mathbb D}=0,qquad \int_{\mathbb D}v^2|1+g|^2=1,
$$
then, with $J$ as in @def-j-functional,
$$
\frac{J(P)}{\pi j^2}=1+S-\sum_{n\ge2}\frac{\rho_n}{(n+1)^2}|g_n|^2+R(g),qquad |R(g)|\le CS^{3/2},
$$
where $j=j_{0,1}$ is the first positive zero of $J_0$, $\rho_n=jJ_{n+1}(j)/J_n(j)$, and $0<\rho_n<2$. In particular,
$$
\frac{J(P)}{\pi j^2}-1\ge S/6.
$$
Moreover, writing $g=t h$ with $t=\sqrt S$ and $\|h\|_{A^2}=1$, the corresponding normalized eigenpair satisfies
$$
\|v-v_0\|_{H^1_0(\mathbb D)}\le Ct,
\qquad |\lambda-j^2|\le Ct^2.
$$
:::

::: {.proof of="lem-disk-perturbation"}
By @def-j-functional, $J(P)=A(P)\lambda_1(P)$; after @def-conformal-data normalizes $A(P)=\pi(1+S)$, it remains to expand $\lambda_1(P)$. The fixed-space expansion in @lem-c1-perturbation supplies the uniform eigenpair branch and remainder. For the quantitative rate, write the pulled-back eigenproblem as
$$
-\Delta v=\lambda|1+g|^2v,\qquad v|_{\partial\mathbb D}=0,
$$
with the weighted $L^2$ normalization. Put $d(z)=1-|z|$. For $g\in A^2$ with no constant or linear term, the Bergman pointwise estimate gives $|g(z)|\le C\|g\|_{A^2}/d(z)$. Consequently, Hardy's inequality gives, for all $\varphi,\psi\in H^1_0(\mathbb D)$,
$$
\left|\int_{\mathbb D}2\operatorname{Re}(g)\varphi\psi\right|\le C\sqrt S\,\|\varphi\|_{H^1_0}\|\psi\|_{H^1_0},\qquad
\left|\int_{\mathbb D}|g|^2\varphi\psi\right|\le CS\,\|\varphi\|_{H^1_0}\|\psi\|_{H^1_0}.
$$
Indeed $|g|^2\le CS/d^2$, $\int|\varphi|^2/d^2\le4\int|\nabla\varphi|^2$, and Cauchy--Schwarz handles the first integral. Therefore the closed forms
$$
q_t[\varphi]=\int|\nabla\varphi|^2,\qquad m_t[\varphi]=\int|1+t h|^2|\varphi|^2\quad(g=th)
$$
form a real-analytic type-(a) family on the fixed domain $H^1_0(\mathbb D)$ for real $|t|$ small (equivalently, a holomorphic two-parameter family in $(t,\bar t)$), with uniform form bounds. The simple disk eigenvalue is isolated by a fixed spectral gap, so the real-analytic form perturbation theorem applies uniformly to this family.

Write $g=t h$ with $t=\sqrt S$ and $\|h\|_{A^2}=1$. The simple disk eigenvalue is isolated by a fixed spectral gap. The form version of analytic simple-eigenvalue perturbation therefore gives, uniformly in such $h$,
$$
v=v_0+t v_1+t^2v_2+O_{H^1_0}(t^3),
\qquad
\lambda= j^2+t\lambda_1+t^2\lambda_2+O(t^3).
$$
The case $S=0$ is the disk and the assertion is immediate, so assume $S>0$. The first variation is $\lambda_1=-j^2\int_{\mathbb D}(h+\bar h)v_0^2=0$ because $v_0$ is radial and $h$ has no constant coefficient. Write $v_0(r)=J_0(jr)/(\sqrt\pi J_1(j))$ and $p_D=j/\sqrt\pi$. For the real mode $h=a z^n$, the first-order equation in the $n$th angular sector has the explicit solution
$$
v_1(r,\theta)=a w_n(r)\cos(n\theta),\qquad
w_n(r)=\frac{r^{n+1}v_0'(r)+p_DJ_n(jr)/J_n(j)}{n+1}.
$$
The Bessel equation verifies the radial equation and $w_n(1)=0$. The second-order solvability condition is
$$
\frac{\lambda_2}{j^2a^2}=-2\pi\int_0^1\left(r^{2n+1}v_0(r)^2+r^{n+1}v_0(r)w_n(r)\right)dr.
$$
Substitution of $w_n$ and one integration by parts reduce this to
$$
\frac{\lambda_2}{j^2a^2}=-\frac{\rho_n}{(n+1)^2},
\qquad \rho_n=j\frac{J_{n+1}(j)}{J_n(j)},\qquad 0<\rho_n<2.
$$
The only nontrivial radial integral is
$$
\int_0^1r^{n+1}v_0(r)J_n(jr)\,dr
=\frac{J_{n+1}(j)}{2\sqrt\pi(n+1)},
$$
which follows by one integration by parts from the Bessel equation. Orthogonality of distinct angular modes and density of analytic polynomials extend the formula to every $h\in A^2$. Since $A(P)=\pi(1+S)$ in @def-conformal-data, this yields the uniform expansion
$$
\frac{J(P)}{\pi j^2}=1+S-\sum_{n\ge2}\frac{\rho_n}{(n+1)^2}|g_n|^2+O(S^{3/2}).
$$
The perturbed branch remains the first eigenvalue by the weighted min--max principle: the mass form $\int|1+g|^2|\varphi|^2$ is positive on nonzero $H^1_0$ functions, and the branch is the positive continuation of the disk ground state. The sine mode is obtained by a phase rotation, and polarization plus density of analytic polynomials extends the second-order form from real monomials to arbitrary complex $h\in A^2$. The Bessel interlacing inequalities $J_n(j)\ne0$ and $0<\rho_n<2$ hold for the first zero $j=j_{0,1}$. Thus
$$
\frac{\lambda}{j^2}=1-\sum_{n\ge2}\frac{\rho_n}{(n+1)^2}|g_n|^2+O(S^{3/2}).
$$
Multiplying by $A(P)/(\pi)=1+S$ from @def-conformal-data produces the displayed $J$ expansion; the cross term $S\sum\rho_n|g_n|^2/(n+1)^2$ is $O(S^2)$ and is absorbed in $O(S^{3/2})$. Since $0<\rho_n<2$, the quadratic term is at least $S/3$; after shrinking the universal small neighborhood, $J(P)/(\pi j^2)-1\ge S/6$. This proves the uniform perturbation expansion and coercivity.
:::

::: {#lem-near-circle-conformal .lemma name="Near-circle conformal deficit" date="2026-10-31"}
For a sequence of admissible stationary $N$-gons in the sense of @def-stationary-polygon whose canonical boundary presentations consist entirely of effective edges, satisfying the edge moments of @lem-edge-moments and with $J,R$ as in @def-j-functional,
$$

$$

$$

\qquad a=|\nabla v_0|^4,
\qquad \int_0^{2\pi}b_1(r,\theta)\,d\theta=0,
\qquad \|R_1\|_{L^1(\mathbb D)}\le CS.

$$

\ge \int_{\mathbb D}a+c_0T-C\{S+\sqrt S\sqrt T+\sqrt S\,T+ST\}.

$$

\le \int_{\mathbb D}a+C\{S+\sqrt S\sqrt T+\sqrt S\,T+ST\}.
$$

$$
T\le C\{S+\sqrt S\sqrt T+\sqrt S\,T+ST\}.
$$

$$

$$
2\pi p_D^4\frac{\beta_n^2}{(n+1)^2(n^2-1)}|a|^2.
$$
Rotational orthogonality removes cross terms, and density of analytic polynomials extends the calculation to $A^2$. The actual relation $g+k=-gk$ then gives
$$
S-T=2\sum_{n\ge2}\frac{\beta_n^2}{(n+1)^2(n^2-1)}|g_n|^2+O(S^{3/2}\sqrt{\log(e/S)}).
$$
The logarithmic inequality
$$
\|L\|_{A^2}^2\le (S+T)/2
$$
comes from $|f|^2+|f|^{-2}-2\ge4(\operatorname{Re}L)^2$ and equality of real and imaginary Bergman energies. Combining these formulas gives
$$
\frac{J(P)}{\pi j^2}\ge1+\sum_{n\ge2}\frac{\beta_n}{(n+1)^2}\left(1+\frac{\beta_n}{n^2-1}\right)|L_n|^2-C S^{3/2}\sqrt{\log(e/S)}.
$$
Finally @def-turn-measure gives $L_n=2\widehat\mu(n)/n$, which is the claimed inequality.
:::

::: {#lem-toeplitz-positive-atoms .lemma name="Positive-atom Toeplitz bound" date="2026-10-31"}
Let $\mu$ be a finite real atomic measure of total mass $1$ with exactly $p$ positive atoms, allowing arbitrary negative atoms. For $0<\tau<1$,
$$
\sum_{n\ge1}\tau^n|\widehat\mu(n)|^2\ge\frac{\tau^p}{1-\tau^p}.
$$
:::

::: {.proof of="lem-toeplitz-positive-atoms"}
Define on $\ell^2(\mathbb N_0)$ the self-adjoint matrix
$$
A_{rs}=\tau^{(r+s)/2}\widehat\mu(r-s)=\sum_iw_i(v_i)_r\overline{(v_i)_s},
\qquad (v_i)_r=\tau^{r/2}e^{-ir\theta_i}.
$$
The Vandermonde vectors at distinct nodes are linearly independent, so $A$ has exactly $p$ positive eigenvalues $\alpha_1\ge\cdots\ge\alpha_p>0$. The trace is $(1-\tau)^{-1}$, and the negative eigenvalues can only decrease the trace, hence $Q:=\sum_i\alpha_i\ge(1-\tau)^{-1}$. The shift compression and the min--max principle give $\alpha_{i+1}\le\tau\alpha_i$. For fixed $Q$ and these ratio constraints, a finite exchange argument (move mass from an earlier coordinate to the latest coordinate until the active constraint is met) shows that the minimum of the strictly convex function $\sum_i\alpha_i^2$ is attained at
$$
\alpha_i=Q\frac{(1-\tau)\tau^{i-1}}{1-\tau^p},\qquad 1\le i\le p.
$$
Consequently
$$
\sum_i\alpha_i^2\ge Q^2\frac{1-\tau}{1+\tau}\frac{1+\tau^p}{1-\tau^p}
\ge\frac{1+\tau^p}{(1-\tau^2)(1-\tau^p)}.
$$
On the other hand,
$$
\|A\|_{HS}^2=\frac{1+2\sum_{n\ge1}\tau^n|\widehat\mu(n)|^2}{1-\tau^2}
$$
and the Hilbert--Schmidt norm dominates the squared positive eigenvalues. Rearranging gives
$$
1+2\sum_{n\ge1}\tau^n|\widehat\mu(n)|^2\ge\frac{1+\tau^p}{1-\tau^p},
$$
which is exactly the claimed bound.
:::

::: {#lem-kernel-comparison .lemma name="Positive kernel comparison" date="2026-10-31"}
For every $n\ge2$, the coefficients in @lem-spectral-core satisfy
$$
0<b_n\le a_n.
$$
Moreover,
$$
b_n=\int_0^\infty e^{-nt}\frac{1-\cos(\sqrt\kappa t)}\kappa\,dt,
$$
so for any signed atomic measure of total mass $1$ with $p$ positive atoms,
$$
E_b(\mu)\ge B_p.
$$
:::

::: {.proof of="lem-kernel-comparison"}
The Bessel bounds $5.78<j^2<5.8$ give $1.89<\kappa<1.9$. The recurrence for $J_n$ implies $0<\rho_n<2$ and, for $n\ge3$, $\rho_n<n\alpha/(n^2+\kappa)$ with $\alpha=\kappa+1$. Substitution into
$$
a_n=\frac{n-\rho_n+\rho_n^2/(n+1)^2}{n^2(n^2-1)}
$$
proves $a_n\ge b_n$; for $n=2$, the identity $J_0(j)=0$ reduces the inequality to $\kappa^3+7\kappa^2+12\kappa-54\ge0$, which holds for $\kappa\ge1.89$.

The Laplace representation follows from
$$
\int_0^\infty e^{-nt}(1-\cos(\sqrt\kappa t))\,dt=\frac{\kappa}{n(n^2+\kappa)}.
$$
Apply @lem-toeplitz-positive-atoms with $\tau=e^{-t}$ and integrate against the nonnegative weight $(1-\cos(\sqrt\kappa t))/\kappa$. Tonelli's theorem gives $E_b(\mu)\ge B_p$.
:::

::: {#lem-signed-turn-lower-bound .lemma name="Signed-turn spectral lower bound" date="2026-10-31"}
For a stationary polygon in the regime of @lem-spectral-core, if $p$ is its number of convex corners, then
$$
\frac{J(P)}{\pi j^2}\ge1+4B_p-C S^{3/2}\sqrt{\log(e/S)}.
$$
:::

::: {.proof of="lem-signed-turn-lower-bound"}
By @lem-spectral-core and @lem-kernel-comparison, $a_n\ge b_n$ for $n\ge2$. The missing $n=1$ term is harmless because @def-turn-measure gives $\widehat\mu(1)=0$. Hence
$$
\frac{J(P)}{\pi j^2}\ge 1+4E_b(\mu)-C S^{3/2}\sqrt{\log(e/S)}.
$$
The lower bound $E_b(\mu)\ge B_p$ is exactly @lem-kernel-comparison.
:::

::: {#lem-two-reflex-exclusion .lemma name="At least two reflex corners are excluded" date="2026-10-31"}
There is $N_1$ such that no stationary admissible $N$-gon in the sense of @def-stationary-polygon, with at least two reflex corners and with $J$ as in @def-j-functional, satisfies
$$
J(P)\le J(R_{N-1})
$$
for $N\ge N_1$.
:::

::: {.proof .draft of="lem-two-reflex-exclusion"}
If there are at least two reflex corners, the number $p$ of convex corners is at most $N-2$. By @lem-near-circle-conformal, $S\le CN^{-3}$, and @lem-signed-turn-lower-bound gives
$$
\frac{J(P)}{\pi j^2}\ge1+4B_{N-2}-o(N^{-4}).
$$
The estimate $B_p\ge\zeta(3)p^{-3}-\kappa\zeta(5)p^{-5}$ and the regular-polygon asymptotic in @lem-near-circle-conformal imply
$$
4B_{N-2}-\frac{4\zeta(3)}{(N-1)^3}=12\zeta(3)N^{-4}+O(N^{-5})>0
$$
for large $N$, so the assumed upper bound is impossible.
:::

::: {#lem-single-reflex-small-atom .lemma name="Single-reflex small positive atom" date="2026-10-31"}
There is a universal $C$ such that a stationary admissible $N$-gon satisfying the edge moments of @lem-edge-moments, with exactly one reflex corner and in the regime of @lem-near-circle-conformal, has an adjacent convex corner $i$ whose turn weight $a=w_i>0$ in @def-turn-measure satisfies
$$
a\le C N^{-9/4}\sqrt{\log N}.
$$
:::

::: {.proof .draft of="lem-single-reflex-small-atom"}
The boundary identity in @def-conformal-data gives a homogeneous $H^{1/2}$ seminorm of $F-F(0)-z$ equal to $S$; restricting it to a straight prevertex arc of length $\varepsilon$ gives a lower bound $c\varepsilon^4$, hence every prevertex gap is at most $CS^{1/4}$. The boundary derivative estimate accompanying @lem-disk-perturbation gives for the disk boundary derivative $p=-\partial_rv$ on every such arc
$$
\operatorname{osc}_I p\le C\{\sqrt S\,\varepsilon\sqrt{\log(e/\varepsilon)}+S\}\le CS^{3/4}\sqrt{\log(e/S)}.
$$

Place the unique negative turn at angle $0$. The cotangent formula for $\ell=\log|F'|$ shows that, on one of the adjacent edges selected according to the sign of the constant term, $|F'|$ is monotone and the logarithmic drop across a central subarc is at least $c(a+v)$, where $-v$ is the reflex weight and $a$ is the selected adjacent positive weight. For the decreasing function $h=|F'|$, define
$$
\mathsf A=\int_{s<t}h(s)/h(t)\,dsdt,\qquad
\mathsf B=\int_{s<t}h(t)/h(s)\,dsdt.
$$
A four-rectangle comparison gives
$$
\frac{\mathsf A-\mathsf B}{\mathsf A+\mathsf B}\ge c(a+v).
$$
Put $k_0=h^{-2}$ and normalize the selected edge to $x\in[0,1]$. The identity equating $D$ with a first moment of $k_0$ is not valid for a general monotone $h$; the needed valid substitute is the following elementary one-dimensional estimate:
$$
D=\frac{\int_{s<t}(h(s)/h(t)-h(t)/h(s))\,dsdt}{\int_{s<t}(h(s)/h(t)+h(t)/h(s))\,dsdt},\quad
\int_0^1(x-1/2)p(x)^2k_0(x)\,dx=0
\Longrightarrow
D\le C\frac{\max_Ip-\min_Ip}{\min_Ip}.
$$
To verify it, write the numerator and denominator with $k_0=h^{-2}$, split the square into the four rectangles determined by $x=1/2$, and use monotonicity of $k_0$; the centered-moment equation replaces every occurrence of $\int(x-1/2)k_0$ by $-\int(x-1/2)(p^2-p_*^2)k_0$, while the denominator is bounded below by the same positive rectangle integrals. Since $p\ge p_D/2$ uniformly, this gives $D\le C\operatorname{osc}_I p$. The lower bound $D\ge c(a+v)$ and the last inequality imply $a+v\le C S^{3/4}\sqrt{\log(e/S)}$. Combining this with $S\le CN^{-3}$ proves the stated bound.
:::

::: {#lem-atom-deletion .lemma name="Deletion preserves the comparison energy" date="2026-10-31"}
Let $P$ be a stationary admissible $N$-gon in the one-reflex regime satisfying $J(P)\le J(R_{N-1})$, with $J,R$ as in @def-j-functional and $\mu$ the one-reflex measure in @def-turn-measure. Let $p=N-1$, and let $a$ be the small positive atom from @lem-single-reflex-small-atom. Put
$$
\widetilde\mu=\frac{\mu-a\delta_{\theta_*}}{1-a}.
$$
Then $\widetilde\mu$ has total mass $1$ and $N-2$ positive atoms, and
$$
E_b(\widetilde\mu)-E_b(\mu)=o(N^{-4}).
$$
:::

::: {.proof .draft of="lem-atom-deletion"}
Let $\delta=E_b(\mu)-B_{N-1}\ge0$. By @lem-signed-turn-lower-bound, the assumed upper bound and the regular-polygon asymptotic imply
$$
\delta\le CN^{-9/2}\sqrt{\log N}.
$$
For $U_b(\theta)=\sum_{n\ge1}b_n\operatorname{Re}(\widehat\mu(n)e^{in\theta})$, the Laplace representation in @def-positive-kernel and Cauchy--Schwarz give
$$
\|U_b\|_\infty\le C\sqrt\delta+CN^{-5/2}.
$$
The exact expansion is
$$
E_b(\widetilde\mu)-E_b(\mu)=
\frac{2a(E_b(\mu)-U_b(\theta_*))+a^2(K_b(0)-E_b(\mu))}{(1-a)^2},
$$
where $K_b(0)=\sum_{n\ge1}b_n$. Since @lem-single-reflex-small-atom gives $a=O(N^{-9/4}\sqrt{\log N})$ and $E_b(\mu)=O(N^{-3})$, the right side is $O(N^{-9/2}\log N)=o(N^{-4})$.
:::

::: {#thm-main-large-n-convexity .theorem .goal name="Large-N low-threshold stationary polygons are convex" date="2026-10-31"}
There is a universal $N_0$ such that, for every $N\ge N_0$, every admissible stationary simple $N$-gon $P$ satisfying
$$
J(P)\le J(R_{N-1})
$$
 is convex. Consequently, no such polygon satisfies $J(P)<m_{N-1}$ while being non-convex.
:::

::: {.proof .draft of="thm-main-large-n-convexity"}
Assume the conclusion fails. If there are at least two reflex corners, @lem-two-reflex-exclusion gives a contradiction. Thus there is exactly one reflex corner. Apply @lem-single-reflex-small-atom and @lem-atom-deletion. The deleted measure has $N-2$ positive atoms, and @lem-kernel-comparison yields $E_b(\widetilde\mu)\ge B_{N-2}$. By the proof of @lem-signed-turn-lower-bound (equivalently, by @lem-spectral-core together with @lem-kernel-comparison),
$$
\frac{J(P)}{\pi j^2}\ge1+4E_b(\mu)-C S^{3/2}\sqrt{\log(e/S)}.
$$
Using @lem-atom-deletion and $S\le CN^{-3}$ from @lem-near-circle-conformal gives
$$
\frac{J(P)}{\pi j^2}\ge1+4B_{N-2}-o(N^{-4}).
$$
The regular-polygon asymptotic gives
$$
\frac{J(R_{N-1})}{\pi j^2}=1+\frac{4\zeta(3)}{(N-1)^3}+O(N^{-5}),
$$
while $B_{N-2}=\zeta(3)(N-2)^{-3}+O(N^{-5})$. Their difference is $12\zeta(3)N^{-4}+O(N^{-5})$, contradicting $J(P)\le J(R_{N-1})$ for large $N$.
:::

# 大 N 非凸排除证明：qmd-prover 重建审计

本目录把附件 `source-original.md` 重建为 `workspace/large-n-proof.qmd`，并用 qmd-prover 的独立 `codex` 检查器配置进行检查：`model: gpt-6.1-sol`、`effort: high`、`citations: standard`、`rigor: standard`。项目保留默认的 unrestricted 外部数学基准；所有非平凡外部结果都在证明文本中点名。

机械检查的最终结果是：22 个语义事实、0 个结构错误、0 个循环、0 个未解析引用；其中 6 个事实因 `.draft` 保持 `open`，其余 16 个尚待独立检查。渲染准备也成功生成了 `.qmd-prover/generated/proof-status.qmd` 和依赖图。

检查器曾对基础定义和 `@lem-edge-moments` 给出通过 verdict；这些记录在后续源文件/外部基准变更后由 qmd-prover 标记为 stale，不能当作当前最终版本的已验证状态。修复后的 `@lem-toeplitz-positive-atoms` 当前缓存检查仍为 `verified`。

Toeplitz 引理的原稿确有错误。原稿写的正谱平方和下界系数不成立；例如 $p=1,\tau=0.9$ 时右端超过实际平方和。已改为
$$
\sum_i\alpha_i^2\ge
\frac{1+\tau^p}{(1-\tau^2)(1-\tau^p)},
$$
并补上了压缩交错、正惯性和严格凸约束最小化的说明。该修复后的引理由 `gpt-6.1-sol/high` 独立检查通过。

原稿中以下接口仍不能诚实地标为已证，因此在 QMD 中保留 `.draft`，主定理也保持 `open`：

- Airy 四次恒等式的全局势函数拼接和角点通量极限；
- 由统一 $W^{1,4}$ 界推出圆盘内包含及统一 $S\le CN^{-3}$ 的近圆定量步骤；
- 加入了独立的 `@lem-disk-perturbation`，把近圆谱展开拆成单独引理，并将 Green 估计改为固定 $H^1_0$ 形式估计；检查器曾对该引理给出 verified，但后续为修复梯度接口而修改了源块，当前缓存需重新确认。
- 新增 `@lem-weighted-disk-resolvent` 和 `@lem-gradient-perturbation` 接口，明确列出从标量谱展开到 $L^4$ 梯度余项所需的加权椭圆估计；检查器仍认为该估计需要进一步证明，因此逆保形导数能量 $T\le CS$ 继续保持 draft；
- 非线性谱下界；
- 单反角小正原子和删除步骤；
- 依赖上述接口的主命题。

其中检查器明确指出：仅有统一 $W^{1,4}$ 界不能直接推出特征函数一致收敛和圆盘内包含；现在已补上紧性、极限识别和内圆包含的定性步骤。谱展开已改用固定 $H^1_0$ 上的形式扰动框架；检查器认为该标量展开在上一版本中可接受，但指出统一余项、Bessel 比值和复模态延拓仍有形式化缺口。检查器还指出原 Airy 证明把“有效边”直接当成所有开边，并且只说局部 Airy 势，未给出全局势和角点边界通量估计。上述问题已在重建稿中补充为显式假设、外部基准或待完成的 draft 接口；没有把它们伪装成已验证结论。

单反角段还修正了一处错误等式：原稿声称一般单调 $h$ 满足
$$
D=2\frac{\int(x-1/2)h^{-2}}{\int h^{-2}},
$$
该等式并不成立。重建稿删除该等式，改用需要单独证明的一维单调权比较估计，并因此保留该引理为 `.draft`。

因此，当前 qmd-prover 状态是：机械层 22 个事实全部通过；`@lem-gradient-perturbation`、逆能量、谱核心及主定理保持 `open`/draft，不能报告整条连续谱链为已证明。附件原稿没有被覆盖，修订语义稿位于 `workspace/large-n-proof.qmd`。
